l: The mysterious Quality, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_a quality of The Tao [mysterious] The mysterious Quality is what The Tao's producing, nourishing, acting without boasting, and presiding without control is called.

l: wheel, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A wheel has thirty spokes united in one nave; its use depends on empty space for the axle.

l: vessels, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: depends_on empty space [their empty hollowness; for their use] The vessels are fashioned from clay, and their use depends on their empty hollowness.

l: apartment, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The apartment is formed by doors and windows cut from walls; its use depends on the empty space within.

l: empty space, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: serves actual usefulness [for actual usefulness] The empty space for the axle, within vessels, and within an apartment enables their use.

l: use, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Use depends on empty space, while what has positive existence serves for profitable adaptation.

l: mind, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: makes_burn vital breath The mind is made mad by the chariot course, wild hunting, and rare and strange objects sought for by people.

l: men, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Men are a group who may come from beneath the sky to rest in the Tao once it has a name, becoming free from failure and error. They dislike being orphans, having little virtue, and carriages without naves. They are taught that increase and diminution can reverse one another. In governing, they are not hurt by departed spirits, yet they do not know the originating principle or authoritative law, and therefore do not know the speaker.

l: sage, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The sage is a person defined by humility, restraint, and care for others. He seeks simple bodily satisfaction rather than the eyes’ endless longing, rejects self-display and striving, and achieves great things precisely by not making himself great. He sets aside excess, extravagance, indulgence, ambition, and purposive action. With no fixed mind of his own, he takes the people’s mind as his own, is good and sincere toward everyone, and treats the people as children. He is still, harmless, straightforward, bright without dazzling, and avoids both sharpness and license. He meets difficulty while it is easy and greatness while it is small, so he avoids difficulties and accomplishes the greatest things without doing what is great. He desires and learns what others neglect, helps the natural development of all things, knows the pain of disease without having it, and knows himself without parading or valuing himself openly. In engagements he does not demand speedy fulfilment. At the end, he does not accumulate: by expending for and giving to others, he possesses more, and in all his doing he does not strive.

l: favour, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Favour is feared as much as disgrace: gaining it brings apprehension of loss, and losing it fear of greater calamity.

l: disgrace, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Disgrace is a feared low position following the enjoyment of favour, and it is regarded as equally feared with favour.

l: honour, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_regarded_as personal conditions [of the same kind as great calamity] Honour is to be regarded as a personal condition, similarly to great calamity. He who honours the kingdom as he honours his own person may be employed to govern it.

l: great calamity, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_regarded_as personal conditions [of the same kind as honour] Great calamity is to be regarded as a personal condition. The body makes a person liable to great calamity; without the body, no great calamity could come to that person.

l: body (which I call myself), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: makes_liable_to great calamity The body is what makes a person liable to great calamity. If the person had not the body, no great calamity could come to the person.

l: kingdom, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The kingdom is a spirit-like thing. It cannot be obtained by active doing: attempts to win it destroy it, and attempts to hold it lose it. It may be entrusted to an administrator who loves and honours it as his own person. When Tao is employed throughout it, men thrive all around.

l: administrator (of the kingdom), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: administers kingdom [with honour and love like that borne to his own person] An administrator who would administer the kingdom while honouring it as his own person may be employed to govern it. One who administers it with the love he bears to his own person may be entrusted with it.

l: the skilful masters (of the Tao), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The skilful masters of the Tao are masters with subtle, exquisite penetration of the Tao’s mysteries, deep beyond men’s knowledge. They appear cautious, irresolute, grave, evanescent, unpretentious, vacant, and dull. By preserving the Tao’s method and not seeking fullness of self, they remain worn rather than new and complete.

l: muddy water, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: becomes_clear clear [when it is left still] Muddy water gradually becomes clear when it is allowed to remain still.

l: movement, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: gives_rise_to condition of rest [gradually] Movement is allowed to go on, and through it the condition of rest gradually arises.

l: condition of rest, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The condition of rest gradually arises when movement goes on.

l: fullness of self, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Those who preserve this method of the Tao do not wish to be full of themselves. Through not being full of themselves, they can seem worn and not appear new and complete.

l: state of vacancy, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: has_degree utmost degree The state of vacancy should be brought to the utmost degree.

l: stillness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Stillness is guarded with unwearying vigour and marks things’ return to their root, reporting fulfilment of their appointed end. It rules movement, overcomes heat, and with Purity gives correct law to all under heaven. Stillness also enables the female to overcome the male and is considered a sort of abasement.

l: root, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_called state of stillness [the return to it] The root is the state to which things in the vegetable world return after their luxuriant growth.

l: unchanging rule, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_a regular rule [unchanging] The unchanging rule is the regular report of the fulfilment of things. Knowing it is intelligence, while not knowing it leads to wild movements and evil issues.

l: knowledge of the unchanging rule, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Knowledge of the unchanging rule produces grand capacity and forbearance, culminating in a community of feeling with all things.

l: community of feeling, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A community of feeling arises from capacity and forbearance, culminating in kingliness of character.

l: kingliness of character, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Kinglyness of character arises from community of feeling and unfolds as becoming heaven-like in character.

l: rulers, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The earliest rulers, in highest antiquity, appeared irresolute through reticence, yet completed their work successfully and let people feel they acted themselves; as faith in the Tao waned, faith in rulers also declined.

l: faith (in the Tao), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Faith in the Tao concerns sufficient faith by rulers or the person making the Tao his business. When it is deficient, people or others come to lack faith in that person; in highest antiquity, people did not know this relation.

l: Great Tao (Way or Method), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_observed not observed [ceased to be] The Great Tao (Way or Method) ceased to be observed.

l: righteousness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Righteousness is a quality that comes into vogue when the Great Tao ceases and appears when benevolence is lost. In its highest form, its possessors always seek to carry it out. It is lost before propriety, after people become filial and kindly.

l: wisdom, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Wisdom, a quality, appears when the Great Tao ceases and benevolence and righteousness arise; it is then presented as something to discard for the people’s benefit.

l: shrewdness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: appears present Shrewdness appeared after benevolence and righteousness came into vogue.

l: great hypocrisy, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: ensues present Great hypocrisy ensued after wisdom and shrewdness appeared.

l: harmony, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: prevails_throughout six kinships [no longer] Harmony no longer prevailed throughout the six kinships.

l: six kinships, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The six kinships were no longer characterized by prevailing harmony.

l: filial sons, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: find_manifestation manifestation Filial sons found their manifestation when harmony no longer prevailed throughout the six kinships.

l: states and clans, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: falls_into disorder The states and clans fell into disorder.

l: disorder, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Disorder occurs in states and clans when the Great Tao ceases to be observed. It increases as people gain more implements to add to profit. Because it is easier to address before it starts, disorder should be prevented before it begins.

l: loyal ministers, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: appears present Loyal ministers appeared when the states and clans fell into disorder.

l: sageness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_a quality [renounced for the people's benefit] Sageness is presented as something that should be renounced for the people’s benefit.

l: methods of government, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: has_quantity three The three methods of government concern renouncing sageness and wisdom, benevolence and righteousness, and artful contrivances and scheming for gain. They are said to have thought olden ways failed in elegance and used names to veil their lack of worth, whereas simple, plain, and true courses would avoid selfish ends and many lusts.

l: learning, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_renounced without troubles [when renounced] Learning is presented as something that can be renounced, with the claim that renouncing it brings no troubles.

l: speaker (the 'I'), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The speaker is listless, still, dejected, and forlorn, with no apparent desires, home, or resting place. Unlike other men, the speaker has lost everything and has a stupid, chaotic, benighted, dull, confused, and incapable mind, drifting as if at sea. Yet the speaker values the Tao as a nursing-mother.

l: multitude of men, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A multitude of men appear satisfied and pleased, as if enjoying abundance and an elevated spring view, having enough and to spare unlike the speaker.

l: fear, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_feared men in general [indeed] Fear is described as something all men experience: what all men fear is indeed to be feared.

l: questions, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Questions ask to be discussed, with a range described as wide and without end.

l: active force, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Active force comes from Tao, which is its only source.

l: things, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Things’ forms, semblances, and essences reside in Tao, forming a beautiful array without decay.

l: nature of the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: explains beauties of existing things [as the basis of knowledge] The nature of the Tao explains how the beauties of existing things endure and remain without decay.

l: completion, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Completion transforms partial into complete, crooked into straight, empty into full, and worn out into new; all real completion is comprehended under this saying.

l: manifestation of the Tao's course, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The manifestation of the Tao's course is an object that people may make their pursuit. Agreement concerning it brings the happiness of attaining to the Tao.

l: person making the Tao his business, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: makes Tao [his business] The person making the Tao his business agrees with people according to whether they pursue the Tao, pursue its manifestation, or fail in both. When he lacks sufficient faith, a lack of faith in him ensues among the others.

l: people pursuing the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: People pursuing the Tao agree with the person making it his business, and through this agreement have the happiness of attaining to it.

l: people making the manifestation of the Tao's course their object, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A group focused on the manifestation of the Tao's course agrees with the person making the Tao his business, and through that agreement attains the happiness of attaining to the Tao.

l: happiness of attaining to the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The happiness of attaining to the Tao is received by those who agree in the Tao, agree in its manifestation, or agree in their failure.

l: person (the one who displays himself, asserts his own views, vaunts himself, or is self-conceited), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A person who displays, asserts, vaunts, or is self-conceited fails to shine, gain distinction, have merit acknowledged, or be allowed superiority.

l: those who pursue the course of the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Those who pursue the course of the Tao reject and do not allow self-display, self-assertion, vaunting, and self-conceit as their course of conduct.

l: conditions of self-display and self-assertion, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: From the standpoint of the Tao, self-display and self-assertion are like remnants of food or a tumour on the body, disliked by all; those pursuing the course of the Tao neither adopt nor allow them.

l: sage king, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The sage king is great and one of the four great things in the universe.

l: Man, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: takes_law_from Earth Man takes his law from the Earth.

l: gravity, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_root_of lightness Gravity is the root of lightness.

l: lightness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: causes_loss_of gravity [when the lord of a myriad chariots acts lightly before the kingdom] Lightness is rooted in gravity. If the lord of a myriad chariots acts lightly before the kingdom, he loses his root of gravity.

l: wise prince, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The wise prince marches all day near baggage waggons, remaining in his proper place and indifferent to brilliant prospects.

l: kingdom, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The kingdom is governed according to Tao and made its own through freedom from action and purpose. Its ruler must be grave and still, never lightly asserting mastery through arms; delight in slaughter cannot achieve one’s will there. Excessive prohibitions and legislation bring poverty, disorder, and theft. Governing a great state requires the care of cooking small fish. Like a low-lying, down-flowing stream, the great state draws small states by condescending and abasing itself, gaining them in order to unite and nourish people.

l: throne, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The throne is lost by the lord of a myriad chariots if he proceeds to active movement.

l: man of skill, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_a master [to be looked up to by person without skill] The man of skill is a master to be looked up to by the person without skill. He is helped by the reputation of the person without skill, who serves as his helper.

l: person without skill, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_a helper [of the reputation of man of skill] The person without skill looks up to the man of skill as a master. He serves as a helper of the reputation of the man of skill.

l: Hiding the light (of his procedure), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: “Hiding the light of his procedure” is the name given to the sage’s skilful saving of every man and thing without casting anything away. Hiding the light (of his procedure) is the practice of first making an expiration before taking an inspiration, strengthening before weakening, raising up before overthrowing, and making gifts before despoiling.

l: The utmost degree of mystery, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: “The utmost degree of mystery” describes the relationship in which the man of skill is honoured as a master and the person without skill serves as his helper.

l: constant excellence, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Constant excellence is retained by one who knows his manhood's strength yet maintains female feebleness, displayed by one who knows how white attracts yet remains within black's shade, and completed by one who knows how glory shines yet loves disgrace.

l: the simple child (the sage), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_a simple child [free from all stains] The simple child is the state reached by maintaining strength with feebleness, and the simple infant man is found in the one who accepts disgrace.

l: man's first state, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Man's first state is returned to by the one who knows how white attracts yet remains within black's shade.

l: the unwrought material, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: forms vessels [when divided and distributed] When divided and distributed, the unwrought material forms vessels.

l: person (the one who would get the kingdom), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A person seeks the kingdom for himself through active doing, but cannot succeed. In trying to win it he destroys it, and in trying to hold it he loses it.

l: course and nature of things, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The course and nature of things reverses conditions: what was in front becomes behind, warmth becomes freezing, strength becomes weakness’s spoil, and stored resources are mocked by ruins.

l: strength, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Strength is often spoiled by weakness and accompanies death. It is false when the mind makes the vital breath burn, and should be mourned; when things become strong, they grow old, contrary to the Tao. The strong is overcome by the weak, does not lead to conquest when relied upon, and has its place below.

l: weakness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Weakness accompanies life from supple birth to firm death and holds a place above.

l: excessive effort, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The sage puts away excessive effort.

l: extravagance, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The sage puts away extravagance.

l: easy indulgence, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The sage puts away easy indulgence.

l: He who would assist a lord of men in harmony with the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: He who would assist a lord of men in harmony with the Tao avoids asserting mastery by force, striking only from necessity, stopping decisively, and guarding against vanity, arrogance, and mastery.

l: lord of men, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The lord of men is the one whom He who would assist a lord of men in harmony with the Tao would assist.

l: mastery, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Mastery is not to be asserted through force of arms or continued operations. The skilful commander avoids completing mastery out of a wish for it.

l: host, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_stationed stationed Wherever a host is stationed, briars and thorns spring up.

l: sequence of great armies, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: has bad years [with certainty] In the sequence of great armies there are sure to be bad years.

l: great armies, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: forms sequence of great armies Great armies are associated with a sequence in which there are sure to be bad years.

l: skilful commander, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A skilful commander assists by striking a decisive blow and then stopping, refusing to continue operations to assert mastery and guarding against vanity, boastfulness, and arrogance.

l: decisive blow, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The decisive blow is struck by a skilful commander, who then stops. It is struck as a matter of necessity, not from a wish for mastery.

l: arms, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Arms are beautiful yet evil omens, hateful to creatures; the superior man uses them only from necessity and does not prize victory through them.

l: creatures, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Creatures live through the One, the Tao; without that life, they would pass away.

l: those who have the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: employs arms [only on the compulsion of necessity] Those who have the Tao do not like to employ arms.

l: superior man, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The superior man honours the left hand except in war, when the right takes precedence. He treats arms as ominous necessities, values calm over forced victory, and grieves bitterly for the multitudes he has killed.

l: war, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: War has a host who commences it and a guest who acts defensively. Though arms may be beautiful, they are evil-omened instruments; war is treated like mourning, with the commander on the right. It should not be entered lightly: when weapons cross, the one who deplores it conquers.

l: victory, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_undesirable_to superior man [by force of arms] Victory by force of arms is undesirable to the superior man. To consider it desirable is to delight in the slaughter of men.

l: slaughter of men, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Delighting in slaughter prevents a person from getting his will in the kingdom; one who has killed multitudes should instead weep for them with bitterest grief.

l: mourning, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: assigns right hand [as the prized position] On occasions of mourning, the right hand is the prized position. The general commanding in chief has his place on the right, according to the rites of mourning.

l: rites of mourning, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The rites of mourning assign the right-hand position to the general commanding in chief. The victor in battle has his place rightly according to those rites.

l: battle, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The victor in battle has his place according to the rites of mourning. He who has killed multitudes of men should grieve for them with the bitterest grief.

l: the world, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The world responds to the Tao and its holders: it dares not deal with one embodying the Tao as a minister, would submit to a feudal prince or king who guards it, and repairs around the holder of the Great Image. It delights in and does not weary of the sage ruler. It also says the speaker’s great Tao appears inferior to other teachings.

l: feudal prince or king, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: guard_and_hold Tao [if able to do so] A feudal prince or king who could guard and hold the Tao would receive the spontaneous submission of all.

l: great rivers and seas, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Rivers and seas receive homage and tribute from all valley streams because they are lower than them, making them kings of the valley streams; their relation to the world analogizes the Tao’s.

l: streams from the valleys, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Rivers and seas receive homage and tribute because they lie lower than those who pay it.

l: valleys, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: are_full full [throughout their void] Valleys are kept full throughout their void through the One (Tao). Without that fullness, drought would parch each vale.

l: other men, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_known a discerning person Knowing other men is described as discernment.

l: self, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A person is intelligent by knowing oneself and mighty by overcoming oneself.

l: others, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_overcome a strong person Overcoming others is described as strength.

l: lot, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_satisfied_with a rich person Being satisfied with one's lot is described as being rich.

l: energy, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_acted_with a person with a firm will [continuously] Acting with energy is associated with continuing to act.

l: will, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_firm a person who goes on acting with energy Continuing to act with energy is said to indicate a firm will.

l: death, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Death is presented as distinct from perishing, and as a grievous reality that people may nevertheless not fear. Its infliction belongs to One who presides over it; those who try to inflict it in One's place risk harm. In a small state, people remain in their own place without intercourse with neighbours until death.

l: perishing, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_absent_after death [for one who dies and yet does not perish] Not perishing after death is associated with longevity.

l: longevity, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_had_by a person who dies and yet does not perish Longevity is attributed to dying without perishing.

l: great achievements, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Great achievements, though great, are considered poor by the person described.

l: holder of the Great Image, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: holds Great Image [in his hands] He holds the Great Image of the invisible Tao in his hands. The whole world repairs around him, and men resort to him without hurt, finding rest, peace, and ease.

l: Great Image, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The Great Image, of the invisible Tao, is held by him who holds the invisible Tao, repairing the whole world and bringing men rest, peace, and ease.

l: the soft, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The soft is a guarded secret of strength and accompanies life. It holds a place above, overcoming the hard; water exemplifies this, though people struggle to put the principle into practice.

l: the hard, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The hard is overcome by the soft. The hard is said to be overcome by the soft.

l: the weak, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The weak overcomes the strong: it is likened to soft, weak water, yet people are unable to carry this out in practice.

l: fishes, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: should_not_be_taken_from the deep Fishes should not be taken from the deep.

l: instruments for the profit of a state, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: should_not_be_shown_to people Instruments for the profit of a state should not be shown to the people.

l: princes, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Princes and kings receive from the One, the Tao, the model for all to follow. Though grand and high, they would decay without moral sway. Therefore, they call themselves Orphans, Men of small virtue, and Carriages without a nave, preferring a coarse appearance like an ordinary stone.

l: transformation, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: becomes_an_object_of desire [if it became to me an object of desire] The transformation of all things through princes and kings could become an object of desire to the speaker.

l: nameless simplicity, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_free_from external aim The nameless simplicity is the expression of desire for the transformation. Simplicity without a name is free from all external aim.

l: propriety, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Propriety is an attenuated form of leal-heartedness and good faith, yet the commencement of disorder. When righteousness is lost it appears; those showing it most highly seek response, then bare the arm and march up when men do not respond.

l: men, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Men delight to exalt the sage ruler, neither feeling his weight above them nor injury from his precedence, and never weary of him.

l: Great man, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The Great man abides by what is solid, rejects what is flimsy, and chooses fruit over flower.

l: spirits, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Spirits receive powers through the One (the Tao); without those powers, they would soon fail.

l: dignity, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: finds_its_root_in meanness [firmly] Dignity finds its firm root in its previous meanness. Princes and kings acknowledge this foundation when they consider themselves mean.

l: all things under heaven, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: All things under heaven sprang from Tao, existing and named.

l: scholars (highest class), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: carry_into_practice Tao [earnestly, when they hear about it] When scholars of the highest class hear about the Tao, they earnestly carry it into practice.

l: One, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: produces Two One was produced by the Tao and produced Two.

l: Two, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: produces Three Two was produced by One and produced Three.

l: Three, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: produces All things Three was produced by Two and produced All things.

l: Breath of Vacancy, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: harmonises All things The Breath of Vacancy harmonises All things.

l: violent and strong, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: does_not_die natural death The violent and strong do not die their natural death. Their fate is made the basis of the teaching.

l: natural death, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The violent and strong do not die their natural death.

l: teaching, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_based_on violent and strong The teaching says that some things are increased by being diminished and others are diminished by being increased. It also takes the fact that the violent and strong do not die their natural death as its basis.

l: the softest thing, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: overcomes the hardest [by dashing against and over] It dashes against and overcomes the hardest.

l: the hardest, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: It is dashed against and overcome by the softest thing.

l: the teaching without words, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_attained_by few in the world Few in the world attain to it.

l: freedom from action and purpose, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The speaker knows its advantage through the softest thing overcoming the hardest and that which has no substantial existence entering where there is no crevice. Freedom from action and purpose is presented as the means by which a kingdom is made one's own.

l: non-action, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Doing nothing on purpose yields advantage; through daily devotion to learning, reaching non-action leaves nothing undone.

l: fame, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_less_great_than life Fame is presented as something a person may value over life, but cleaving to fame means rejecting what is more great. Pursuing fame can bring sorrow and pain nearer.

l: life, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Life is valued above fame and wealth; losing wealth while preserving life avoids greater sorrow, while contentment and knowing when to stop support long life.

l: the state, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_richer_than stores The state is associated with reproach that a person may accept and thereby be hailed as its altars' lord.

l: vigour, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: endures long Vigour endures for a long time when great achievements are regarded as poor.

l: cold, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Cold is overcome by constant action.

l: heat, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Heat is overcome by being still.

l: Purity, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: gives correct law [to all under heaven] Purity and stillness give the correct law to all under heaven.

l: correct law, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The correct law for all under heaven is given by Purity and stillness.

l: swift horses, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Swift horses are sent back to draw dung-carts when the Tao prevails in the world.

l: war-horses, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: breed_in border lands [when the Tao is disregarded in the world] When the Tao is disregarded in the world, war-horses breed in the border lands.

l: ambition, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Ambition is described as something whose sanction constitutes no guilt greater than it.

l: one's lot, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Discontent with one's lot is described as no calamity greater than it.

l: wish to be getting, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The wish to be getting is described as no fault greater than it.

l: sufficiency of contentment, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The sufficiency of contentment is enduring and unchanging, presented through Tao prevailing in the world.

l: one (generic observer), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A person understands all that takes place under the sky and sees the Tao of Heaven without leaving his door or window; going farther out from himself brings less knowledge.

l: Way of Heaven, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The Way of Heaven can be seen without looking outside one’s window. It is compared to bending a bow: lowering what is high, raising what is low, diminishing superabundance, and supplementing deficiency. It has no partiality of love, yet always stands with the good man. Though possessing all sharpness, it does not injure.

l: knowledge, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Knowledge can be obtained without travelling.

l: sages, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The sages possess knowledge without travelling, correctly name unseen things, and accomplish their ends without intending to do so.

l: he who devotes himself to learning, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: He devotes himself to learning, seeking day by day to increase his knowledge.

l: learning, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Learning involves seeking from day to day to increase knowledge.

l: he who devotes himself to the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: He who devotes himself to the Tao diminishes doing day by day, arrives at non-action, and thereby does everything.

l: doing, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Doing is diminished again and again until he arrives at doing nothing on purpose.

l: all under heaven, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: All under heaven considers Tao most valuable because it is obtainable by seeking and may let the guilty escape guilt; yet obtaining all under heaven requires giving oneself no trouble, since taking trouble prevents possessing it.

l: he who gets as his own all under heaven, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: He gets all under heaven as his own by giving himself no trouble with that end, unfolding through devotion to learning.

l: mind, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The sage has no fixed mind of his own; he makes the mind of the people his mind. His mind remains in a state of indifference to all.

l: Men, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Men come forth and live, then enter again and die. Of every ten, three are ministers of life, three ministers of death, and three aim to live while moving toward the land of death.

l: life, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Life is entrusted to a person for a time. Excessive endeavours to perpetuate life can cause movements toward the land of death. Life is associated with softness and weakness. Man is supple and weak at birth, while trees and plants are soft and brittle in early growth.

l: death, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Death is the fate Men enter after living. Some act as ministers of death, and the land of death is approached by those whose efforts to perpetuate life are excessive. Death is associated with firmness and strength. At death, Man is firm and strong, while trees and plants are dry and withered.

l: he who is skilful in managing life, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A person skilled in managing life when entrusted with it. From coming forth to living, he travels land unafraid of rhinoceros or tiger and enters a host without avoiding weapons, because no place of death is in him.

l: rhinoceros, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: finds_no_place_in he who is skilful in managing life [into which to thrust its horn] The rhinoceros cannot find a place in he who is skilful in managing life into which to thrust its horn.

l: tiger, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: finds_no_place_in he who is skilful in managing life [in which to fix its claws] The tiger cannot find a place in he who is skilful in managing life in which to fix its claws.

l: sharp weapon, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A sharp weapon cannot find a place to admit its point in one skilful in managing life, as people come forth, live, enter again, and die.

l: mother (The Tao), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_mother_of children (the mother’s children) The mother is found as the source from which one knows what her children should be. Guarding the qualities of the mother that belong to one keeps one free from all peril to the end of life.

l: children (the mother’s children), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The children are what one comes to know when the mother is found.

l: one, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: One is a child of The Tao and should guard the mother’s qualities. Keeping the mouth closed and nostril portals shut brings freedom from laborious exertion; opening the mouth and promoting affairs through breath brings no safety. Guarding the mother’s qualities keeps one free from peril to life’s end.

l: light, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Light is used well by reverting to its bright source, warding blight from the body and hiding the unchanging from men.

l: princes, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Princes maintain fine courts while neglecting fields and leaving granaries nearly empty; they wear elegant robes and swords, indulge in food and drink, hold excessive wealth, and are called robbers and boasters.

l: robbers and boasters, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Princes who display luxury while neglecting fields and granaries may be called robbers and boasters. Their conduct is contrary to the Tao.

l: boastful display, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_feared most [by the speaker when conducting a government according to the Great Tao] Boastful display is identified as what someone conducting a government according to the Great Tao should be most afraid of.

l: family, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A family ruled by Tao gains riches, while sons extend sacrifices to its shrine.

l: neighbourhood, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A neighbourhood where Tao prevails abounds in thriving, as observed across different cases.

l: he who has in himself abundantly the attributes (of the Tao), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_like infant He who has in himself abundantly the attributes of the Tao is like an infant.

l: infant, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The infant abundantly embodies Tao: though its bones are weak and sinews soft, its grasp is firm. It shows an excited virile member, cries all day without hoarseness, has harmonious and perfect physical essence, and is unharmed by poisonous insects, fierce beasts, and birds of prey.

l: harmony, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Harmony is shown by the infant's ability to cry all day without its throat becoming hoarse. Knowing this harmony reveals the unchanging Tao.

l: becoming strong and old, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Becoming strong and old is contrary to Tao, and whatever is contrary to Tao soon ends.

l: knower of the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A person who knows Tao and, by disposition, does not speak of it. He shuts his mouth and nostril-portals, tempers sharpness and brightness, unravels complications, and joins others’ obscurity. Entering Mysterious Agreement, he transcends familiarity, distance, profit, injury, nobility, and meanness, becoming the noblest man under heaven.

l: Mysterious Agreement, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_a agreement [mysterious] The Mysterious Agreement is the name for blunting sharp points, unraveling complications, attempering brightness, and bringing oneself into agreement with the obscurity of others.

l: people, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The people are portrayed as living ordinary lives yet thoughtlessly indulging in them, without fearing death or what they ought to fear. They are warned that this failure will bring their great dread and are urged not to grow weary of the conditions sustaining life. Though they know that softness overcomes hardness and weakness strength, they cannot put this into practice. Their condition also worsens as prohibitive enactments multiply, making them poor. Under the sage’s purposeless action, stillness, lack of trouble, and lack of ambition, they are said to become correct, rich, and primitively simple.

l: correction, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: becomes distortion [by a turn] Correction may by a turn become distortion, and the good within it may become evil.

l: crafty dexterity, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Crafty dexterity is used with weapons of war and, as men possess more of it, brings forth more strange contrivances.

l: prohibitive enactments, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: increase poverty [when multiplied in the kingdom] The multiplication of prohibitive enactments increases the poverty of the people.

l: poverty, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_increased_by prohibitive enactments [when multiplied in the kingdom] Poverty among the people increases when prohibitive enactments multiply.

l: legislation, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: increases thieves and robbers [when more legislation is displayed] The more display there is of legislation, the more thieves and robbers there are.

l: moderation, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Moderation regulates human constitution, renders proper service to the heavenly, and alone effects an early return to man’s normal state.

l: the human (in our constitution), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The human (in our constitution) is regulated by moderation.

l: early return (to man's normal state), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Early return to man's normal state is effected by moderation, repeatedly accumulating the attributes of the Tao.

l: attributes of the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The attributes of the Tao are repeatedly accumulated in the early return to man's normal state. Their repeated accumulation brings the subjugation of every obstacle to such return.

l: subjugation (of every obstacle to such return), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Subjugation of every obstacle to such return arises through repeatedly accumulating the Tao’s attributes; its limit remains unknown.

l: ruler of a state, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A ruler of a state may be one who does not know the limit of subjugation, framed as regulating humans under a constitution.

l: state, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: has_mother mother of the state The state is associated with the ruler who may arise through not knowing the limit of the subjugation. Possessing the mother of the state allows one to continue long.

l: mother of the state, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_a mother [of the state] The mother of the state is possessed by one who may continue long. Its case is compared to a plant with deep roots and firm flower stalks, securing enduring life.

l: manes of the departed, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: have spiritual energy [though it is not manifested] When the kingdom is governed according to the Tao, the manes of the departed do not manifest their spiritual energy. They do not employ that energy to hurt men.

l: spiritual energy, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_employed_to_hurt men [not] The spiritual energy of the manes of the departed exists but is not manifested or employed to hurt men when the kingdom is governed according to the Tao.

l: good influences, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: converge_in virtue of the Tao [when the manes and the ruling sage do not injuriously affect each other] The good influences of the manes of the departed and the ruling sage converge when they do not injuriously affect each other.

l: virtue of the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The virtue of the Tao is where the good influences converge when the manes of the departed and the ruling sage do not injuriously affect each other.

l: small states, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Small states flow toward the great state; by abasing themselves, they win it over and seek to be received by and serve it.

l: female, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: overcomes male [by her stillness] The female is used as an example of overcoming the male through stillness.

l: abasement, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Abasement is associated with stillness and produces different results depending on who practices it. For a great state it leads to gaining adherents, while for a small state it leads to procuring favour.

l: the sovereign, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The sovereign occupies his place as Son of Heaven, appoints three ducal ministers, and values a lesson of Tao above a great offering.

l: the way of the Tao, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The way of the Tao acts without thinking of acting and conducts affairs without trouble; it treats small as great, few as many, tastes without discerning flavour, and recompenses injury with kindness.

l: injury, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_recompensed_with kindness [by the way of the Tao] In the way of the Tao, injury is recompensed with kindness.

l: kindness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Kindness is given in recompense for injury.

l: greatness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Greatness arises from smallness; the sage accomplishes the greatest things by acting before they become great.

l: smallness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Small things are treated as great in the way of the Tao. The sage does things while they are small, before they become great.

l: that which is at rest, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_easy_to_keep_hold_of thing [when at rest] That which is at rest is easily kept hold of.

l: thing, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A thing is easiest to address before it indicates its presence; while at rest it is easily held, brittleness invites breaking, and smallness dispersal.

l: order, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: should_be_secured_before disorder [before disorder has begun] Order should be secured before disorder has begun.

l: success, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Success is a point at which people often ruin their affairs when they are on its eve.

l: beginning, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The beginning is the point at which care should be exercised if affairs are not to be ruined at the end.

l: other men, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Other men desire things that the sage does not desire and prize things difficult to get. They learn what the sage does not learn.

l: multitude of men, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The multitude of men has passed by what the sage turns back to.

l: natural development of all things, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The sage helps the natural development of all things and does not dare to act with an ulterior purpose of his own.

l: ancients, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Ancients skilled in practising Tao sought to make people simple and ignorant rather than enlighten them.

l: knowledge, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Much knowledge among the people is said to create difficulty in governing them.

l: governor, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: govern state [by wisdom] The governor who knows the two principles concerning wisdom and non-use of wisdom follows their model and rule. Such a governor possesses mysterious excellence.

l: wisdom, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Trying to govern a state by wisdom is described as a scourge to it.

l: model and rule, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The two principles about governing provide a model and rule for the person who knows them.

l: mysterious excellence, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Mysterious excellence is the deep, far-reaching ability to know and follow the model and rule; it makes its possessor seem opposite to others while leading them into great conformity with the possessor.

l: three precious things, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A precious things has three parts: gentleness first, economy second, and shrinking from taking precedence of others third.

l: gentleness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Gentleness enables boldness, brings victory in battle, maintains its ground, and protects its possessor through Heaven’s saving power.

l: economy, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Economy enables liberality; abandoning it while seeking liberality moves one toward death.

l: shrinking from taking precedence of others, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: enables_highest_honour highest honour [by becoming a vessel] Shrinking from taking precedence of others enables the speaker to become a vessel of the highest honour. Giving up the hindmost place and seeking to be foremost leads to death.

l: wars (Tao's wars), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: belongs_to Tao Tao's wars concern a skilled figure who avoids martial display and rage. Victory is achieved without separation from foes, and strength comes through non-contention.

l: ideal warrior-leader (Tao's wars), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The ideal warrior-leader in Tao's wars avoids martial display and rage, fights with good will, vanquishes foes while keeping apart from them, and humbly practices his art. He fulfills men's wishes, unites them by bending their wills, and gains power through never contending.

l: master of the art of war, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A master of the art of war advises against starting conflict or aggressive advance, preferring defensive action, withdrawal, and deploring war.

l: calamity, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_greater_than lightly engaging in war [no calamity is greater] Lightly engaging in war is described as the greatest calamity.

l: gentleness, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_precious precious [the gentleness that is nearly lost by lightly engaging in war] Gentleness is described as precious and at risk of being lost through lightly engaging in war.

l: words (the speaker's words), The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Words called very easy to know and practise contain an originating, all-comprehending principle and authoritative law, yet no one in the world both knows and practises them.

l: originating and all-comprehending principle, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The originating and all-comprehending principle is present in the speaker's words. Men do not know it.

l: authoritative law, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: governs things The authoritative law is present in the speaker's words and governs the things the speaker enforces. Men do not know it.

l: knowledge and knowing, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Knowing while recognizing one does not know is the highest attainment; thinking one knows without knowing is a disease.

l: disease, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The disease is the condition of thinking one knows when one does not. Being pained at having it preserves a person from it.

l: pain, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: is_inseparable_from disease Pain at having the disease preserves a person from it. The sage understands that this pain would be inseparable from the disease.

l: great dread, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: comes_on people [when they do not fear what they ought to fear] The great dread will come upon the people when they do not fear what they ought to fear.

l: ordinary life, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Ordinary life should not be indulged in thoughtlessly. Weariness does not arise when such indulgence is avoided.

l: man who dares wrong, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: A man boldly dares to do wrong in defiance of the laws and is put to death.

l: man who does not dare wrong, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The man who does not dare to do wrong lives on, with boldness appearing in his restraint.

l: net of Heaven, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Heaven’s net has large, far-apart meshes, yet its bold reach lets nothing escape.

l: One, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: presides_over death [always, in its infliction] One presides over the infliction of death. A person who inflicts death in the room of One is compared to someone hewing wood instead of a great carpenter and may cut his own hands.

l: people, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: The people suffer famine as superiors consume many taxes. Excessive agency by superiors makes them difficult to govern, while great labour to obtain living means leads them to make light of dying.

l: famine, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Famine is suffered by the people because of the multitude of taxes consumed by their superiors.

l: taxes, The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics
s: Taxes are multitudinous, consumed by superiors, and cause the people to suffer famine.
